title: stability-first-rollout-blueprint-and-quick-prototyping-notes
summary: Working notes for a ‘stability-first’ rollout UX concept: lightweight operator controls that bias early traffic to conservative model variants, surface latency and correctness guardrails, and provide a compact runbook for emergency fallback. Includes wireframe microcopy, edge cases, and backlog tickets for prototype MVP.
body:
Context and motivation:
- Problem: product teams deploy model updates frequently; failures are rarely total but manifested as latency spikes, degraded relevance, or sporadic hallucinations. Current console flows emphasize percentage traffic split but don't make safety-first defaults obvious.

Stability-first concept (short):
- Default strategy for new rollouts: prioritize safety/latency over feature exposure.
- Core controls surfaced up-front: safety budget (error rate tolerance), latency SLOs, model compatibility pins (quantized vs fp16), and automatic fallback policy.

Operator journey (happy path):
1) Create rollout -> pick baseline & candidate models -> choose strategy: Stability-first (default) / Aggressive / Experimentation.
2) Stability-first applies: start at 1% traffic, parallel health probes (latency/response-quality), conservative caching TTLs, KV cache warm-up.
3) System waits for two green probe windows (configurable: 2 x 5min).
4) Auto-advance increments: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with metric gates.
5) If gate fails, console shows immediate rollback suggestion and one-click fallback (route to baseline or to degraded-but-fast variant).

Wireframe notes (screen-by-screen, rough):
- Create rollout modal: small header, dropdown for strategy, inline help text: "Stability-first: minimize disruption; will auto-fallback on latency or quality regressions."
- Metrics preview strip (mini cards): latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost delta, QA score change (from eval set). Each card has a tooltip and a threshold toggle.
- Control panel: manual override slider (0-100%), speed toggle (conservative/normal/fast), safety budget numeric input. Copy: "Safety budget = allowed % of failing requests before auto-fallback"
- Incident view (during rollout): big red banner + one-click routes: Pause | Rollback | Divert to baseline | Divert to degraded. Microcopy: "Traffic is being diverted to fallback due to p95 > 1200ms for 3 windows."

Microcopy samples (to iterate):
- Strategy description: "Stability-first: Automatically stages traffic and protects latency and correctness. Choose this for customer-facing endpoints."
- Safety budget helper: "Set a tolerance for failed responses (latency/timeouts/QA regressions). When exceeded, the rollout will revert automatically."
- Fallback explanation: "Fallback can route to a previous model, a quantized fast variant, or a degraded mode (shorter max tokens)."

Edge cases & questions (need engineering input):
- How to surface blended requests where only some tokens timed out? (should we mark as error?)
- When using function-calling, how to ensure deterministic fallbacks that keep schema?
- How to present partial degradations (e.g., model returns text but hallucination score is high)?

Runbook (operator quick steps):
- If rollout shows p95 > configured SLO for 2/3 windows -> console banner + suggested action: Divert to baseline.
- For hallucination/quality regressions (QA score drop > threshold) -> Pause + notify owners + snapshot N examples.
- If metrics disagree (latency ok but QA bad) -> route 5% of traffic to canary and rate-limit endpoints that trigger hallucination (if detected by classifier).

MVP scope (prototype to ship):
- UX: Create rollout modal, metrics strip, manual override, incident banner, one-click fallback.
- Backend: metric gate evaluation engine (configurable windows), simple fallback router to baseline or degraded variant, probe harness for QA eval using customer prompt set.
- Observability: token-level cost delta, per-route p95, QA sample capture.

Backlog tickets (prioritized rough):
- R1: ROLL-4201: Build create-rollout modal + strategy selector + microcopy.
- R2: ROLL-4202: Implement automatic gate evaluation service (5m windows).
- R3: ROLL-4203: One-click fallback routing + UI incident banner.
- R4: ROLL-4204: Probe harness for customer prompt sets (QA scoring).
- R5: ROLL-4205: Small-scale A/B visualization (comparison of candidate vs baseline across metrics).

Prototype interaction notes (quick sketches translated to words):
- Hover over metric card opens a mini-chart with time window selector (last 5/30/120 minutes).
- Dragging the manual slider should immediately show simulated impact on traffic mix and estimated cost delta.
- Confirmation modal for rollbacks should show last 5 traces that triggered the gate.

Open design decisions (for product/eng discussion):
- Default safety budget value (1%? 0.1%?) and how to communicate risk.
- Whether automatic fallback should be auditable in the deployment log (yes, must include triggers and snapshots).
- Interaction with cached responses: when candidate returns similar cached prefix, gate logic should ignore cached hits.

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Design: produce 2 high-fidelity frames for Create Rollout modal and Incident banner (owner: Marisol).
- [ ] Eng: quick spike on gate evaluation latency and probe harness (owner: Chen).
- [ ] PM: refine default safety budget and write release notes copy (owner: Asha).
- [ ] UX research: 3 quick sessions with SRE / ML infra users to validate microcopy and default flows (owner: Liam).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could expose a compact DSL for power users: sequence: start@1/5m -> wait@2x5m -> promote@20 -> fallback:on-fail. But keep the console simple for MVP.
- Consider an experimental "degraded mode" label that explains to customers that responses may be concise but faster.

References and inspiration:
- Internal: rollout-safety-matrix (confluence), evals-runbook-2025.
- External: canary rollout patterns from k8s/cri, feature flag platforms that offer percentage-based rollouts and automatic rollback on error rates.

End of notes. This is a working doc — messy bits intentionally left in as prompts for grooming and pairing with engineering spikes.
